name: SavaPato Uptime Monitor
author: macha795

sections.description:
SavaPato Uptime Monitor monitors the uptime of your websites by regularly checking registered URLs and sending email notifications when downtime is detected.

Key Features:

  • Register multiple URLs to monitor
  • Run periodic health checks at a configurable interval
  • Receive email notifications on downtime detection
  • Receive email notifications when a site recovers from downtime
  • Register multiple notification email addresses
  • Down detection based on consecutive failures (reduces false positives)
  • Plan-based monitor limits and minimum check intervals
  • View monitoring history (recent Up/Down check results at a glance)
  • View monitoring status from the admin dashboard


Free plan:

  • Monitor up to 3 URLs
  • Check interval: every 5 minutes (minimum)
  • 7 days of monitoring history
  • URL monitoring
  • Status detection (Up / Down)
  • Consecutive failure count
  • Keyword check (contains / does not contain)
  • WP-Cron automatic scheduling
  • Email notification on downtime
  • Recovery notification
  • Test email
  • Manual Cron trigger
  • Environment diagnostics

Pro plan (additional):

  • Up to 30 URLs (Starter: 5 / Standard: 20 / Business: 30)
  • Check interval: every 1 minute (minimum)
  • Up to 365 days of history (Starter: 30 / Standard: 90 / Business: 365 days)
  • Send notifications to multiple email addresses at the same time.
  • On subscription expiry, monitors are disabled (not deleted) and preserved.

External Services

This plugin integrates with Freemius (https://freemius.com) to handle licensing and payments for the Pro version.

Free version: The Freemius SDK is included solely to display upgrade and pricing information within the admin dashboard.
The free version skips the account connection and does not connect to Freemius servers during normal use.
Clicking “Upgrade Now” opens the Freemius checkout page in your browser.

Pro version: Freemius connects to its servers for license activation, plan management, and account-related operations.
Data that may be sent: site URL, WordPress version, plugin version, admin email address, and license key.
No personally identifiable information beyond the admin email is collected without your consent.

Privacy policy: https://freemius.com/privacy/
Terms of use: https://freemius.com/terms/
sections.installation:
1. Go to ‘Plugins’ > ‘Add New Plugin’ in your WordPress admin.
  2. Search for ‘SavaPato Uptime Monitor’ and click ‘Install Now’.
  3. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  4. Configure monitored URLs and notification settings via the ‘SavaPato’ admin menu.
sections.changelog:
16.5.6

  • Added keyword check for URL monitors. You can now verify that a specific keyword is present (or absent) in the response body — useful for detecting errors that return HTTP 200, such as maintenance pages.
  • Added support for multiple notification recipients (Pro). You can now send downtime and recovery alerts to up to 5 email addresses simultaneously. Free plan supports 1 recipient.
  • Added a “Compare Plans” page to the admin dashboard, showing a side-by-side feature comparison of all available plans.
  • Improved database migration reliability. Version numbers are now updated only after each migration step succeeds, preventing stuck states on failed upgrades.

16.5.5

  • Added a monitor history page. Click the “History” button next to each monitor to view recent Up/Down check results, including the checked time, HTTP status code, response time, and any error messages.
  • Added plan-based history retention periods.
  • Added site name and site URL to downtime and recovery notification emails, making it easy to identify which site triggered the alert when managing multiple sites.

16.5.4

  • Adjusted the downtime detection logic.
  • Adjusted the link display in the plugin list.

16.5.3

  • Added an upgrade page to the admin dashboard. You can now upgrade to the Pro version directly from within the admin panel.

16.5.2

  • Added plan-based monitor limit. Free plan supports up to 3 monitors; paid plans support up to 5–30.
  • Added plan-based minimum check interval. Free plan supports intervals of 5 minutes or more; paid plans support as low as 1 minute.

16.5.1

  • Initial release.
